blocks.c: Holt McCallany and Jonathan Groff show a crime scene photo to someone off-screen in Mindhunter.

blocks.x: Netflix didn't produce a third season of the cult hit series Mindhunter, but seven years after the show's abrupt ending, the streamer has released a psychological thriller movie that picks up from where it left off. Like Mindhunter, which follows a team of FBI profilers conducting state-of-the-art investigations into the psychology of mass murderers, the new movie revolves around the study of a future terrorist's mind. Russell Crowe plays a Harvard professor who conducts scientific experiments on a young Ted Kaczynski, who is played in the film by former child star Jacob Tremblay.

The two appear prominently in one of the film's two parallel storylines, with the other focusing on the FBI's decades-long manhunt for Kaczynski, later dubbed the Unabomber. In the second storyline, Shailene Woodley appears as the lead investigator handling the Unabomber case. Directed by Janus Metz, the new movie opened to poor reviews, standing in contrast to the filmmaker's earlier work on shows such as Andor and True Detective. It also stood in stark contrast to another movie starring Crowe, released around the same time. The other film, The Weight, debuted theatrically and emerged as Crowe's top-rated title in nearly three decades, according to the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes.

Great villains choose their opponents carefully. Something about you got their attention.

What do you actually believe about right and wrong?
Every nemesis is really an argument about the thing you believe most.

AThere are lines. Mine are private and absolute.
BRules are the only thing keeping us from being animals.
CMorality is a system, and systems can be solved.
DThings happen. Most of it was never up to me.

What finally gets under your skin?
Everybody has a pressure point. Finding yours is the whole plan.

ABeing seen clearly by somebody I cannot read.
BWatching good people do something ugly.
CLosing to someone who was simply better prepared.
DHaving no move left that changes anything.

They have made their move. How do you fight back?
This is the part of the film where the audience finds out who you are.

ACarefully, and never where they expect to be touched.
BLoudly. I would rather lose than play their game.
CWith a better plan. I can out-think this.
DDirectly, once, with whatever is closest to hand.

What would they use against you?
A good villain never brings a weapon you have not already handed them.

AMy privacy. I have kept far too much to myself.
BMy conscience. I will not cross the line they want.
CMy ego. I cannot resist a worthy opponent.
DMy certainty that I can handle it alone.

What do they actually want from you?
The money is never the point. Something else always is.

ATo understand me better than anyone ever has.
BTo prove I am no better than they are.
CTo finally be beaten by someone worth the trouble.
DNothing at all. I stepped into the wrong path.

How does it end between the two of you?
Eight questions in, this is the one that decides who comes for you.

AA conversation I will be replaying for years.
BA choice forced on me that has no clean answer.
COne final move, and the better mind wins.
DA coin in the air, and nothing I can say.

Russell Crowe's New Movie Is the Latest in Netflix's Streak of Mid-Budget Hits This Year

While The Weight holds a "Certified Fresh" 94% Rotten Tomatoes score, Crowe's Unabomber is sitting at a 26% score on the website. Despite the poor reception, the film delivered 16 million views in its opening week of release. According to the latest edition of Netflix's weekly viewership report, Unabomber retained its crown as the streamer's most-watched movie, adding another 24 million views between September 28 and October 4. This puts the film's total views at 40 million, which means that it qualifies as the latest in Netflix's stellar streak of mid-budget hits this year. It comes on the heels of fellow genre movies such as War Machine, The Rip, Thrash, Apex, The Last House, and more recently, The Whisper Man. Several of these films were able to hit the coveted 100-million-views mark, and Unabomber seems primed to join them.
Stay tuned to Collider for more updates.
